title: The ball as the least densely packable convex solid
decision_reason: Precise pre-draft fingerprint, independent scholarly corroboration, seven resolution-scope comparisons, separated A62 self-review and rendering/link checks passed. No unresolved material matching resolution claim located.

problem_fingerprint.objects: Every compact convex body K in R^3 with nonempty interior; no symmetry, smoothness or polyhedral assumption.
problem_fingerprint.packing: A locally finite family of sets a_i+Q_i K with a_i in R^3 and Q_i in O(3), whose interiors are pairwise disjoint. Reflections as well as translations and rotations are permitted, as in K15's full-isometry convention.
problem_fingerprint.density: For a packing P, use the limsup as R tends to infinity of the volume fraction of the radius-R ball centered at the origin occupied by the union of its members. Let delta(K) be the supremum over all such packings.
problem_fingerprint.target: Prove or disprove delta(K)>=pi/sqrt(18) for every such K. The benchmark is the optimal packing density of congruent balls.
problem_fingerprint.scope: Unrestricted congruent packing, including nonperiodic arrangements; not lattice-only, translative-only, random close packing or a finite-container objective. Only one shape and one size in each packing. No characterization of the equality case is added.
problem_fingerprint.family_policy: One global shape-comparison problem. Local near-ball, symmetric, fixed-shape and alternative-density variants do not create additional entries.

independent_corroboration.qualification: The two reviews share authors with each other; they supply one independent author group relative to Kallus. Both explicitly retain the global question.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Determines the maximum density of congruent balls in R^3.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Sets the benchmark for one shape; gives no lower bound for every convex shape.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: There is a uniform small neighbourhood of B in which origin-symmetric nonellipsoidal convex solids have strictly greater lattice density.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Both origin symmetry and closeness matter; arbitrary far-from-sphere or nonsymmetric bodies are outside the theorem.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: The lattice statement excludes ellipsoids; affine invariance leaves their lattice density equal to the sphere value. Remark 1 combines other results for unrestricted symmetric local packing.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Do not strengthen the lattice statement to all nonspherical bodies. This entry asks only the weak global inequality and not uniqueness of equality.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: For each nonspherical K in minimal-mean-width position, double-lattice density increases along (1-lambda)B+lambda K for 0<lambda<lambda_0(K).
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The allowable parameter interval depends on K; this is neither a uniform neighbourhood nor a global statement at lambda=1. Double lattices permit point inversions, covered by O(3).

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: A first-order perturbative calculation for random packing protocols assumes isostatic sphere packings, suitable deformation behavior and orientation minimization.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Different observable and additional modeling assumptions; it cannot establish the supremum over all congruent packings for all shapes.

resolution_comparisons.locator: Section I and Theorem 1, Section II.D, p.7
resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Explicit regular-tetrahedron double-dimer packing with density 4000/4671, above the sphere benchmark.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: The earlier tetrahedron counterexample suggestion is excluded by an explicit lower bound; this does not solve exact tetrahedron optimality or all convex shapes.

resolution_comparisons.result_scope: Identity for a weighted combination of spherical-sector volume fractions derived from a fixed FCC cell decomposition.
resolution_comparisons.comparison_with_target: Two kinds of interstitial units and a fixed arrangement replace the single arbitrary convex body and unrestricted optimum; no general Ulam proof or counterexample is claimed.

nearest_existing_entries.difference: Exact maximum density of one fixed regular tetrahedron; this entry compares every convex body to the sphere. Its tetrahedron instance already satisfies the lower bound, while the exact fixed-shape optimum is unknown.
Quadratic nearest-point distortion of point configurations and Voronoi cells, not volume occupied by nonoverlapping congruent solids.
Minimum volume of a single constant-width body, with a width constraint and no assembly-density optimization.

normalization_checks: Dimension is exactly three; no planar or higher-dimensional analogue is counted.
K is compact, convex and full-dimensional. All copies have the same size.
O(3) includes reflections, matching the source full-isometry definition; translations are a_i. No SO(3)-only strengthening.

The occupied-volume upper density agrees with K15 volume(K) divided by lower mean cell volume: only copies intersecting a fixed-width boundary shell differ between the two counts. A fixed inscribed-ball radius bounds their number by O(R^2), negligible after division by volume(B_R).
The sphere benchmark is pi/sqrt(18). No strict inequality for nonspheres or equality classification is added.
The applied paragraph identifies reflections/mirror shapes and does not claim a random-jamming, finite-container or dynamical guarantee.
